claims.claim: Asking a rating question displaces the probed internal state; the rating is weakly coupled to the pre-question probe but strongly to the post-question probe.
claims.quoted_support: We find that rating questions displace the probed state, and that the rating is only weakly coupled with the probe score before the question but tracks the post-question probe much more strongly.

breadth.confidence_families: numeric self-report of affective states vs linear probes; verbalized confidence only mentioned in intro (Sec 1)
breadth.elicitation_formats: rating question at Post/Next/Prior; retrospective, third-person, user variants (App. A.3)
breadth.calibration_metrics: not present (correlation of rating with probe)
breadth.causal_intervention: steering along probe direction changes ratings (Sec on steering)

claims.claim: Rating-probe relationship is not concept-specific and does not improve with scale from 1B to 27B.
claims.quoted_support: ratings are associated with other concepts’ probes as much as with their own, and change little when the question is about the user. Finally, neither the pre-question coupling nor concept specificity improves with scale (1B–27B).
